user_story: As the archive curator, I want a live countdown to the Feb 1, 2026 launch, so that I can see at a glance how much time remains.
expected_behavior: On load and every 60 seconds (setInterval in updateCountdown), the page computes the diff between now and a hardcoded launch date new Date('2026-02-01T00:00:00') and writes days/hours/mins into #countdown-days/#countdown-hours/#countdown-mins. If the diff is <= 0 it shows 0/0/0. The label hardcodes 'until Feb 1, 2026'.
test_notes: Open features/status-report/index.html via a local server (it is an ES module importing ./script.js and ./data.js, so file:// will fail on CORS). The countdown placeholders start as em-dashes and should fill within a frame. Note: the launch date is past (today is 2026-06-21), so the countdown will read 0/0/0.
code_smell: Launch date is hardcoded and already in the past (2026-02-01); the report still markets 'February 2026 launch readiness' so the whole page now reads as stale/expired with a 0/0/0 countdown.

user_story: As the archive curator, I want top-level counts (records, entities, relationships, verified %) on cards, so that I can summarize archive scale quickly.
expected_behavior: renderOverviewCards builds four cards from STATUS_METRICS: totalRecords, totalEntities, totalRelationships (all .toLocaleString()), and verifiedPercent as '<n>%' with a sublabel of verifiedRecords. The verified card's number color is chosen by threshold: emerald >=90, amber >=70, else rose (current data 73.6% -> amber). Injected via innerHTML into #overview-cards.
test_notes: Open the page and confirm four cards render with values 869 records, 5,736 entities, 7,489 relationships, 73.6% verified (640 records). Data is static from data.js, not fetched.
code_smell: Color class is built with a template string `text-${card.color}-600`; this only renders if Tailwind already includes text-emerald-600/text-amber-600/text-rose-600 in the prebuilt dist/tailwind.css (dynamic class names are not JIT-generated at runtime), so a card color can silently fall back to unstyled.

user_story: As the archive curator, I want per-field completeness shown as tiered progress bars, so that I can spot which metadata fields are lagging.
expected_behavior:
renderFieldCompleteness iterates FIELD_COMPLETENESS.tier1..tier4, and for each field renders a label, a progress bar whose fill width = field.complete% and whose color class is emerald >=90 / amber >=70 / rose otherwise, plus a right-aligned percentage. The function overwrites the card's inner HTML including its own '

Field completeness

' heading.
test_notes: Open the page; the 'Field completeness' card should show four named tiers each with field rows and animated-width bars. Confirm bar colors track the thresholds.
code_smell:
The static markup in index.html already contains an '

Field completeness

' inside #field-completeness, and renderFieldCompleteness prepends another identical

when it sets innerHTML, so the heading appears once but is duplicated in source intent (the JS heading replaces the static one).

user_story: As the archive curator, I want quality metrics as pass/warn/fail badges, so that good and bad metrics are visually distinguished.
expected_behavior: renderQualityMetrics renders five rows: verified %, categorized %, has-summary (= 100 - missingSummaryPercent), missing categories %, missing concepts %. 'good' metrics use emerald/amber/rose by >=90/>=70/else; 'bad' metrics (missing*) invert to emerald/amber/rose by <=10/<=30/else. Each value is shown via .toFixed(1) + '%' in a .badge span.
test_notes: Open the page; the 'Quality metrics' card should show five labeled rows with colored badges. Badge classes (badge-emerald/amber/rose) are defined in shared-styles.css (linked via ../../shared-styles.css).
code_smell: 'Has summary' is computed as 100 - missingSummaryPercent rather than read directly, so any rounding in the precomputed missingSummaryPercent propagates into the displayed completeness figure.

user_story: As the archive curator, I want bar charts of entity types, top relationship types, and era distribution, so that I can see the shape of the extracted graph and the time coverage.
expected_behavior: renderBarChart (shared) draws horizontal CSS bars scaled to the max value in the dataset. It is called three times: entity-chart from ENTITY_TYPES (type/count, violet #7c3aed), relationship-chart from RELATIONSHIP_TYPES (type/count, sky #0284c7, section labeled 'top 10'), and era-chart from ERA_DISTRIBUTION (era/count, green #059669). Returns early if the container is missing or data is empty.
test_notes: Open the page; three bar-chart sections (Entity type distribution, Relationship types, Era distribution) should each render labeled rows with proportional bars and right-aligned counts.
code_smell: renderBarChart injects item[labelKey] directly into both the title attribute and the row text without escaping. Source data is trusted static data.js, but unlike the data-explorer and dataviz tools this one has no escapeHtml helper, so it is inconsistent with the project's own XSS hardening.

user_story: As a developer auditing the report, I want every imported dataset to actually render, so that the report is not silently dropping a metric.
expected_behavior: script.js imports CATEGORY_DISTRIBUTION from data.js but never references it again. No category-distribution chart or section is rendered anywhere; the 'Era distribution' section uses ERA_DISTRIBUTION instead.
test_notes: Grep confirms CATEGORY_DISTRIBUTION appears only on the import line. There is no #category-chart container in index.html. Nothing to click; this is a dead-data finding.
code_smell: Dead import: CATEGORY_DISTRIBUTION is loaded but never used, implying an intended category chart was dropped or never wired up. Either render it or remove the import.

user_story: As the archive curator, I want a release checklist and a launch timeline, so that I can track readiness items and milestones.
expected_behavior: renderChecklist maps CHECKLIST_ITEMS to rows with a status icon: 'complete' (green check), 'in_progress' (amber clock), else a dashed pending circle; optional note shown in parentheses. renderTimeline maps TIMELINE_MILESTONES to dated timeline rows with a dot colored by status: complete=green, current=amber, else pending grey.
test_notes: Open the page; the 'Release checklist' card lists items with status icons and the 'Launch timeline' card lists dated milestones with a vertical connector. Both are static from data.js.

user_story: As the archive curator, I want prioritized action items I can expand for detail, so that I can drill into outstanding work.
expected_behavior: renderActionItems maps ACTION_ITEMS to cards showing a count, title, and a priority badge (high=rose, medium=amber, low=emerald) plus a border/background tint by priority. Clicking the header calls global toggleExpand(index), which toggles the .open class on .expandable-<index> (CSS animates max-height 0 -> 500px) and rotates the chevron icon 180deg.
test_notes: Open the page, scroll to 'Action items', click a card header; its description should expand below a divider and the chevron should rotate. Click again to collapse.
code_smell: Expanded content is capped at max-height:500px in the inline CSS; an action item with a long description would be clipped. Low risk with current short descriptions.

feature: Remote CSV load and verified-record filtering
user_story: As a researcher, I want the explorer to load the archive records and keep only verified ones, so that the visualization reflects trustworthy data.
expected_behavior: On window.onload, fetchDataAndInitialize parses a hardcoded Google Sheets published-CSV URL (csvUrl) via PapaParse (download:true, header:true). Headers are normalized to lowercase/underscore; only ALLOWED_COLUMNS are retained; tags/thematic_categories/key_concepts are split on commas and semicolons. Records are kept only if verified===TRUE and id and a non-empty title (.filter(r => r.isVerified && r.id && r.title.trim())). Errors (network, parse, empty, no-verified) call handleError, which shows '(Error loading data)' in the header and a red message in the info panel, then dismisses the tutorial modal.
test_notes: Open tools/active/dataexplorer/data_explorer_grid.html. It fetches a live docs.google.com CSV, NOT a local data path, so it requires internet and the sheet being published; offline it shows '(Error loading data)'. The record count text should read '(N records in a 441-dot grid)' on success.
code_smell: The data source is a hardcoded Google Sheets published-CSV URL (not the archive's own data/ JSON), so this tool is out of sync with the rest of the site's data pipeline. The changelog claims a v2.5.0 remote->local CSV fallback to RosenArchivedataset-TEST-DATA.csv, but the actual HTML has no fallback logic and no such local file exists — a documented-but-missing feature, so a Google Sheet outage takes the tool fully down.

feature: Date-sorted dot grid with placeholder padding
user_story: As a researcher, I want records laid out as a chronological grid of dots, so that I can perceive the archive across time and pick a starting record.
expected_behavior: processData deep-clones verified records, sorts ascending by publication_date, slices to targetMax, and pads the remainder with placeholder dots (createPlaceholderRecord) so the grid is always a perfect square (441 or 625). Dots are placed on a fixed 900x1150 canvas with 25px padding; X/Y coordinates are recorded for path snapping. Verified dots are full opacity; unverified/placeholder dots render at 0.3 alpha and are not hoverable or clickable.
test_notes: After the data loads and you click 'Explore the archive', the canvas shows a square grid of colored dots (earliest top-left). Hovering a verified dot grows it 50% and shows a tooltip; placeholder/dimmed dots do not respond.
code_smell: Dot color is derived from a char-code hash of the first concept/category value modulo the palette size, not from a real category->color mapping, so the legend's category colors do not actually match the dots they describe (the legend is decorative, not authoritative).

user_story: As a researcher, I want to switch whether connections are drawn by key concepts or thematic categories, so that I can explore different relational lenses.
expected_behavior: The header <select id='connectionField'> calls updateConnectionField on change with 'key_concepts' or 'thematic_categories'. That sets the active field, re-runs processData (recoloring dots), re-renders the color key label, and calls resetView to clear any active exploration. Both connections and dot colors always use the same field (unified) for consistency.
test_notes: Change the 'Connect dots by:' dropdown; dot colors should recompute and any drawn lines should clear. The color key heading updates to 'Dot color is determined by: Key concepts' / 'Thematic categories'.

feature: Exploration mode: click a dot to draw animated connections
user_story: As a researcher, I want clicking a record to reveal up to 15 animated paths to related records, so that I can trace its connections without clutter.
expected_behavior: Clicking a verified dot calls selectPrimaryRecord: it locks the view, dims unrelated dots (FADE_OPACITY 0.15), finds verified records sharing at least one value in the active field, caps them at MAX_CONNECTIONS_TO_SHOW (15), and animates a 3-segment grid-snapped Manhattan path to each over a random 1200-2800ms duration. Lines are colored by the shared value's hash. In locked mode only the primary and connected dots are clickable; clicking the primary or a connected dot refreshes the info panel; clicking empty space or 'Clear the board' calls resetView.
test_notes: Click any colored dot; the info panel slides up, the orange 'Clear the board' button appears, and animated right-angle lines draw to related dots. Click empty canvas to reset. Header text changes to '(ID <id> connections shown)'.
code_smell: Connections are derived from at most the first MAX_CONNECTIONS_TO_SHOW matches in array order (slice after filter), not ranked by relevance/shared-value count, so a record with many connections shows an arbitrary subset.

feature: Hover tooltips for dots and connection lines
user_story: As a researcher, I want hovering a dot or a line to show context, so that I can understand a record or why two records are connected without clicking.
expected_behavior: mousemove hit-tests dots (getHoveredRecord) and, in locked mode, lines (checkLineHit within HIT_TEST_THRESHOLD px). Dot tooltip (renderDotTooltipContent) shows date reformatted to DD-MM-YYYY, title, and first 3 tags. Line tooltip (renderLineTooltipContent) shows 'Shared concept' or 'Shared thematic category' plus the shared value. Hovering a line dims all other lines/dots to DIMMED_OPACITY (0.25). Tooltip follows the cursor with scroll offsets. All interpolated values are escaped via escapeHtml (issue #157).
test_notes: Hover a dot to see date/title/tags; enter exploration mode then hover one of the animated lines to see the shared value and watch other lines dim.
code_smell: Date formatting blindly reorders the YYYY-MM-DD parts to DD-MM-YYYY; any non-ISO or partial date (e.g. just a year) is left as-is, producing inconsistent date display across dots.

feature: Floating info panel with minimize/maximize and view-source
user_story: As a researcher, I want a resizable detail panel for the selected record plus a list of its connections, so that I can read full metadata and jump to sources.
expected_behavior: The bottom floating panel (togglePanelState) supports closed/default(30vh)/minimized(52px, shows title)/maximized(full screen, shows ID) via the red/yellow/green control dots; double-clicking the active state reverts to default. updateInfoPanel renders title, author/date/source, pull quote, era, thematic-category pills, summary, key concepts, tags, and a date-sorted 'Connected records' list (max-h-96) with per-row 'View source' links. The header 'View record source' button is shown only when sanitizeUrl returns a valid http(s) URL; otherwise hidden. All URLs pass through sanitizeUrl (http/https only) and all text through escapeHtml.
test_notes: Select a record, then click the yellow dot (collapses to a title bar) and green dot (full-screen modal); the red dot closes and clears the board. Confirm 'View record source' opens in a new tab only for records that have a URL.
code_smell:
The tutorial modal copy contains stray HTML in the bullet list (an orphan and unbalanced tags inside a

) — cosmetic, but the markup is malformed.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to expand the grid to show more dots, so that I can see more of the archive at once.
expected_behavior: The full-width bar below the canvas (toggleGridSize) switches currentMaxDisplay between MIN_RECORDS_TO_DISPLAY (441, 21x21) and MAX_RECORDS_TO_DISPLAY (625, 25x25) and updates its label between 'Show 625 total dots' and 'Hide 625 total dots'. Toggling reuses cached verifiedMasterRecords (isToggle short-circuit) so it does not re-fetch the network.
test_notes: Click the grey bar under the canvas; the grid should grow to 625 slots and the label flips to 'Hide 625 total dots (Click to contract)'. No network re-request occurs on toggle.
code_smell: Both grid sizes (441/625) can exceed the verified-record count, so the extra slots are filled with non-interactive placeholder dots; on a small dataset most of the grid is empty filler, which can mislead about archive size.

user_story: As a first-time user, I want an intro modal while data loads, so that the tool feels responsive and explains itself before I start.
expected_behavior: An opaque #tutorialModal shows on load with explainer text and an 'Explore the archive' button. handleExploreClick dismisses the modal only once isDataLoaded is true; if clicked early, the button switches to 'Loading data...' and disables, and the completed parse auto-clicks it to dismiss. On data error, handleError also forces the modal to dismiss so the user is not trapped.
test_notes: Reload the page and immediately click 'Explore the archive' before data lands; the button should show 'Loading data...' then auto-dismiss when ready. With no network, it should still dismiss to an error state rather than hang.
code_smell: The auto-click re-dismiss path keys off exploreButton.textContent === 'Loading data...'; if that label string is ever changed in one place but not the other the modal could fail to auto-dismiss — a brittle string-coupling.

feature: Load archive JSON with optional entity graph and lazy full summaries
user_story: As a researcher, I want the dashboard to load the same archive data the site uses, so that the charts reflect the real (non-social) records.
expected_behavior: On DOMContentLoaded, fetchData loads ../../../data/archive-core.json (required) and ../../../data/archive-entities.json (optional, .catch->null) in parallel. Core load failure shows 'Could not load archive data.' with the escaped error. Records with type==='social' are excluded; each record is mapped (date->publication_date, pub->original_publication, categories->thematic_categories, summaryPreview->summary, Concept entity names->key_concepts) and kept only if it has id, title, and a finite year. A malformed entity graph is caught so the rest of the dashboard still works (key-concepts chart just stays empty). After first paint, loadFullSummaries fetches ../../../data/archive-details.json and patches full summaries in place, re-filtering only if a search is active.
test_notes: Open tools/active/dataviz/dataviz.html through a local server from the repo root so ../../../data/*.json resolves (paths are relative and resolve identically locally and under /j/rosen-archive/). The spinner should replace with the dashboard once archive-core.json loads. Note: archive-core.json is ~13 MB, so first load is slow.

feature: Filters: keyword search, year range slider, category and publication checkboxes
user_story: As a researcher, I want to filter records by keyword, year range, category, and publication, so that I can narrow the dataset to what I am studying.
expected_behavior: updateDashboard recomputes state.dashboardData by AND-combining: year within the noUiSlider range; ANY selected thematic category (OR within categories); publication in the selected set; and a debounced (300ms) case-insensitive search matched against title, summary, and joined key_concepts. Category checkboxes list all unique categories; publication checkboxes list the top 10 publications by count. 'Reset all filters' clears the slider to full range, unchecks all boxes, and empties the search. Every filter change refreshes stat cards, all charts, and the table (resetting to page 1).
test_notes: With the dashboard loaded, type in 'Keyword search', drag the year slider, and tick category/publication boxes; stat cards, charts, and the table should all update live. Click 'Reset all filters' to restore the unfiltered view.
code_smell: Search only upgrades to full summary text after archive-details.json (~13 MB) finishes loading in the background; until then search runs against the ~120-char preview, so early searches can miss matches with no visible indication that summaries are still partial.

user_story: As a researcher, I want headline stats for the current filter, so that I can read scale and time span at a glance.
expected_behavior: updateStatCards shows: filtered record count (localized), years covered as 'min - max' (or 'N/A' when empty), unique publication count, and most active year (mode of year counts, or 'N/A'). All four recompute on every filter change.
test_notes: Apply any filter and watch the four stat cards (Filtered records / Years covered / Publications / Most active year) update. With an over-restrictive filter they should read 0 and 'N/A'.

feature: Four interactive charts with CDN-failure resilience
user_story: As a researcher, I want charts of themes over time, top publications, top concepts, and yearly activity, so that I can see trends visually.
expected_behavior: updateAllCharts (no-op if Chart.js is unavailable) rebuilds four Chart.js charts from the filtered data, destroying the prior instance first: thematic-focus (stacked line of top 5 categories per year), publications-treemap (chartjs-chart-treemap, color-hashed tiles, tooltip '<pub>: <n> records'), top-concepts (horizontal bar of top 10 key concepts), and yearly-activity (bar of records per year). Chart.js, the treemap plugin, and noUiSlider all load from CDNs with SRI integrity hashes; each is guarded so a blocked/failed CDN degrades gracefully (charts/slider skipped, table and filters still work).
test_notes: With data loaded, all four chart canvases should render and re-render as filters change. To test resilience, block the jsdelivr/cdnjs hosts; the dashboard should still show stat cards, filters, and the table without the charts or slider.
code_smell: The 'Top key concepts' chart depends on archive-entities.json; if that file is missing or has no Concept entities the chart renders empty with no in-UI explanation (only a console.warn), so a user may think there are no concepts rather than that the graph failed to load.

user_story: As a researcher, I want a sortable, paginated table of the filtered records, so that I can scan and order the underlying rows.
expected_behavior: renderDataTable shows Date / Title / Publication columns. Clicking a header sorts by that column (toggles asc/desc, default desc on column change) with an active arrow indicator and resets to page 1. rows-per-page selector offers 10/25/50/100. Pagination controls show 'Showing X to Y of Z results' with Prev/Next buttons (disabled at the ends); when results fit on one page it collapses to 'Showing N results'. An empty result set shows a 'No data available for the selected filters.' row.
test_notes: Click the Date/Title/Publication headers to sort, change 'Rows per page', and use Prev/Next. Over-filter to confirm the empty-state row appears.
code_smell: Sort comparison uses raw < / > on values; for the Date column publication_date is an ISO-ish string so lexical order usually matches chronological order, but any non-ISO or empty date will sort incorrectly and empties drift to one end.

feature: Export filtered records to CSV with formula-injection guard
user_story: As a researcher, I want to export the filtered records as a CSV, so that I can analyze them in a spreadsheet.
expected_behavior: exportDataToCSV alerts 'No data to export...' when the filtered set is empty. Otherwise it builds a CSV with headers id, publication_date, title, original_publication, summary, key_concepts, thematic_categories (array fields joined with '|'). Each cell passes through escapeCsvCell, which prefixes a leading apostrophe when the cell starts with a formula trigger (= + - @ tab CR LF) and RFC-4180 quotes when needed (issue #423). The Blob downloads as rosen_archive_export_<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv.
test_notes: Apply a filter then click 'Export filtered data (CSV)'; a dated file should download. With an empty filter result, the button should alert instead of producing an empty file. Open the CSV and confirm any formula-like cell is prefixed with an apostrophe.
